title: What Comes Next?
description: A skip list is a sorted linked list with express lanes built over it, and a coin flip decides which values get one. No rotations, no rebalancing, and still O(log n) — which is why Redis uses one for every sorted set it keeps.
long_description:
A balanced tree is fast because somebody wrote the rotations. A skip list is fast because of coin flips.

The bottom level is an ordinary sorted linked list, and it is the only level that holds every value. Each value above it is there because a coin came up heads, then heads again — so about half the values have a second level, a quarter have a third, and one or two reach the top. Those upper levels are express lanes over the list.

A search starts at the top left and walks right until the next value would overshoot the target, then drops a level and does it again. The wall counts the comparisons it takes and, beside it, the comparisons the bottom walk would have taken.

Nothing here is staged: the heights are flipped, and both counts on screen are the real ones for the value actually searched for.
action_hints: watch the coin flips decide how tall each value gets
slow it down to follow the search dropping levels
compare the two comparison counts at the end
deal new data for a different set of express lanes
